Yes. You add us to your repository as a collaborator, and we read the code before quoting any change. If there is no code yet, order MVP Build instead, which starts from nothing.
How do we agree what each feature does?
We write a short description with the screens, rules and edge cases, and you approve it before we code. That keeps arguments about what was meant out of the process.
Which languages and frameworks do you work in?
Mostly JavaScript and TypeScript with React or Next.js and Node, plus Python and PHP on request. Tell us your stack in the order form and we confirm before you pay for anything.
Will the new features break what already works?
We run your existing tests and add our own, and we work on a separate branch. Nothing reaches your live product until you have reviewed and merged it.
desc:
Custom SaaS core feature development adds the workflows that make your product worth using, such as projects, invitations, uploads, search and notifications. Ecom Swift LLC builds and tests each feature in your existing codebase and delivers it as a pull request.

## What are core features in a SaaS product?

Core features are the actions a customer comes to your product to perform, as opposed to supporting pieces like a settings page. In a project tool they are creating projects, assigning tasks and inviting teammates. In a document product they are uploading files, searching and sharing.

Custom feature development means a developer adds those actions to the code you already have, following its structure, instead of starting over.

## Why half-built apps stall

Many products stop at the prototype stage. The login works and the layout looks right, but the central action is incomplete, buggy or missing. The owner cannot show it to customers, so there is no feedback, and without feedback it is hard to justify more investment.

Features added carelessly create a second problem. Code pasted in without regard for the existing structure makes the next change harder. Data fields get added without migrations, forms accept anything, and errors show up as blank screens. A feature is only finished when it handles the unhappy paths too.

## How features translate into results

Users judge a product by whether it does the job. A completed workflow lets a prospect go from idea to outcome in one session, and that moment is what turns a trial into a habit. Notifications bring people back at the right time. Search and filters keep the product usable once there is more than a handful of records.

For you, working features mean demos that land and early customers who can actually try the thing. Each feature reviewed through a pull request also keeps your team in control of the code, so nothing arrives as a mystery.

## What good feature work includes

- A written description of the behavior, agreed before coding starts.
- Changes limited to the parts of the app that the feature touches.
- Data model updates with safe, reversible migrations.
- Form checks and clear error messages in plain language.
- Loading, empty and failure states, not only the happy path.
- Permission checks, so users reach only their own data.
- File uploads with size and type limits.
- Email or in-app notifications where they make sense.
- Search and filters on a list that will grow.
- Tests for the new behavior, with an automated suite available as an add-on.

## How we work in your codebase

We read the code first, then write the feature behavior in plain sentences for you to confirm: who can do it, what they see, and what happens when something goes wrong. Only then do we build, using the languages, libraries and naming habits your project already follows.

Each feature arrives as a pull request in your repository, so you can read the change, ask questions and merge when ready. The Basic package covers one feature with a short note. Standard covers a connected set of features, migrations, validation and demo videos. Premium covers a larger set with notifications, search, uploads and a technical handover.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe each feature as a user action with a clear start and finish.
- Keep a branch or staging copy so changes can be tried safely.
- Review each pull request while it is small.
- Decide in advance what happens when input is wrong.
- Back up your database before schema changes.

**Avoid:**
- Asking for several loosely defined features in one request.
- Skipping review because the demo looked fine.
- Editing the same files at the same time as the developer.
- Storing uploaded files without size or type limits.
- Adding features nobody has asked for yet.

## Who this service is for

Founders with a prototype generated by a no-code tool or an earlier freelancer often need the core workflow finished properly. Small teams whose developer is busy on other work can use it to add a self-contained piece of the product. Agencies maintaining a client app can bring in extra hands for one defined feature.

## What we need from you

Repository access as a collaborator, a description of the feature in your own words, and a list of any examples or screens you want to follow. We never need your passwords, and we prefer to work on a branch so your main code stays untouched until you approve each change.
